title: The letter A
hookLine: Shingon meditation on the Sanskrit letter A, the sound of all beginnings

cards: Ah. Open your mouth and let the breath out, and that's the sound that comes. No tongue against teeth, no lips pressing.
Babies make it. Doctors ask for it with a little wooden stick. People sigh it when the hot bath is just right.
It might be the plainest sound a person can make. Shingon took that sound, and the letter that writes it, and set it at the center of a meditation: a single letter on a white moon, on a lotus.
That letter is today's word: A.

teach.h: A COMES FIRST, AND HIDES IN ALL.
teach.b: Shingon teachers point out that in the Indian alphabet A stands first, and that every consonant is read with a hidden a sound after it unless a mark silences it.
So the A, they say, is in every sound, the way the open breath is underneath every word.
The Mahavairocana Sutra, which Shingon treasures, links the letter A with the teaching that all things are unborn from the beginning.
Shingon reads it this way: before any thing appears, before any word is shaped, there is an origin that was never made and never ends.
The A points to it, and the plainest sound becomes a sign for the ground of everything. The practice is called ajikan, contemplation of the letter A.

teach.h: A LOTUS, A MOON, A LETTER.
teach.b: Tradition associates it with Kukai's school, and the image is simple: a lotus; on the lotus, a full moon disc, white and round; on the moon, the letter A, written in an old Indian script.

teach.h: THE WHOLE MAP IN ONE SOUND.
teach.b: The practitioner gazes at the image, breathes, and lets the sound and the shape of A fill the mind, until the moon seems to grow, and the letter with it. Why so small?
Yesterday's mandalas were crowded with buddhas, a whole world painted. Today's is one letter.

In Shingon, both carry the whole teaching. The vast map and the single sound are not two, the way the womb world and the diamond world are not two. A person who can't take in a whole mandala can still breathe out ah.

how: Shingon practitioners practice ajikan, contemplating the Siddham letter A on a moon disc above a lotus while breathing and sounding A; it is also taught to lay people as an introduction to Shingon meditation.

games.q: you can't take in a whole crowded mandala. what does Shingon offer instead?
o: one letter, A, on a moon.
games.why: ajikan: a lotus, a moon, a single letter, and the open breath. the small image holds the whole teaching.

practice: Take a slow breath in, and on the out-breath let the sound come, quietly or only in your mind: ah, as long as the breath is and no longer.
Breathe in again, and again, ah, and if you'd like, picture a round white moon in front of you as you do it. If you lose the sound, start the next breath fresh; there's nothing to get right.

wordCard.voice: The letter A. In Shingon, the first letter and the sound inside every sound, a sign that all things are unborn from the beginning, and the heart of ajikan. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit a, the first letter. Shingon pictures it in the older Siddham script; this is the Devanagari form.

carryVoice: Your line: ah. The whole map, held in one plain and open breath. See you tomorrow.
